text:
Jordan Lee: Quick GA callout — were launching the Cost-Aware Adaptive Fallbacks feature for Hosted API today. This lets requests specify cost/latency/quality preferences and the platform will automatically route to the best available variant (including quantized fallbacks) while preserving SLA tiers. Rolling out regionally over ~2 hours. :rocket:
Maya Gupta: big win. What's the user-visible surface? any header flags or new console pages?
Jordan Lee: Console: Settings -> Routing Policies -> Cost-Aware Fallbacks (new UI). API opt-ins: `X-Redwood-Prefer: cost|latency|quality` and `X-Redwood-Routing-Trace: 1` for sampled routing traces. Also a new per-route policy JSON you can bind in the Console.
Alex Rivera: SLA and billing impact? customers worried about silent downgrades to cheaper variants.
Sam Holt: SLA note: we guarantee the tiered latency/availability targets — fallbacks never downgrade an SLA-backed account below their committed tier. Billing: normal inference billing applies; using cheaper fallback variants reduces unit cost. Exported routing traces (RoutingDump) are opt-in and billed under "debug-exports".
ops-bot: runbook + rollback: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/cost-aware-fallbacks. Alerts: if fallback-rate > 7% for SLA customers sustained 10m or p95 token-latency +25% for 5m, escalate. Canary keys: cafb-canary-01..06. Auto-rollback rules in runbook.
Maya Gupta: Dedicated / Private customers?
Jordan Lee: Dedicated: toggle available in Admin -> Feature Flags -> CostAwareFallbacks; cluster operators can pin allowed fallback families. Private: included in the 2.1.0 on-prem package; operators must run the routing-agent upgrade and the policy-migration tool (link in docs).
sla-bot: Note: Accounts with Enterprise SLAs will have an explicit enforcement flag that prevents cost-only fallbacks. If you are a sales/CS owner of an SLA account, check the migration page.
docs-bot: Docs live: https://docs.redwood.ai/cost-aware-fallbacks (migration guide, policy JSON schema, examples for curl/SDKs, and recommended defaults)
Alex Rivera: any breaking changes to existing endpoints?
Jordan Lee: No breaking changes. Existing requests will default to previous routing behavior. To opt into adaptive fallbacks include `X-Redwood-Prefer` or set a route policy in Console. We will not auto-migrate customers. Deprecation: old toggle `enable_fallbacks_v1` will be removed on 2026-09-30 — migration tools provided.
Maya Gupta: ops question  will this add extra load when probing fallbacks?
Sam Holt: probing is rate-limited and async; we run lightweight health checks and maintain cached performance profiles. Expect minor control-plane load during rollout; we've provisioned capacity. Watch control-plane error rates and the route-probe-latency metric.
Alex Rivera: can we get a short curl example to share in eng channels?
Jordan Lee: sure:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Prefer: cost" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Routing-Trace: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"mosaic-3b","input":"Draft a 150-word blurb about the new feature."}'
```
Maya Gupta: marketing/comms? we should coordinate messaging about cost controls and SLA protections.
Jordan Lee: Product + Marketing will draft customer emails, a blog post, and a changelog entry. CS will get a targeted list of accounts affected by the deprecation toggle removal.
ops-bot: QA checklist and pre-rollout tests are linked in the runbook. Perf canaries scheduled for the first two US regions.
Alex Rivera: who to ping if something breaks during rollout?
Sam Holt: Ping @eng-sre oncall and add the canary key to the alert. We also have a scheduled office hours AMA at 16:30 PT in #product for migration questions.
Jordan Lee: final: please do not flip the global toggle manually unless you're on the rollout team. Thanks everyone 9 :white_check_mark:
